reason: H0 exclusively exercises JSON decoding and does not compile or invoke the CRC64 module, so it cannot reach the slicing-by-8 implementation in ecma_hasher.update! or validate its stateful hashing semantics. The new length-8 loop plus length-1 remainder path makes input lengths and update partitions around multiples of eight fuzz-worthy.
evidence: H0 defines WUFFS_CONFIG__MODULE__AUX__JSON and WUFFS_CONFIG__MODULE__JSON, but no CRC64 module macro.
H0 calls wuffs_json__decoder__decode_tokens and wuffs_aux::DecodeJson; it never constructs or calls ecma_hasher.
S1 changes ecma_hasher.update! to iterate with length: 8 and advance: 8, reading p[0x00] through p[0x07], followed by an else path with length: 1.
S1 expands ECMA_TABLE from roarray[1] to roarray[8] and indexes ECMA_TABLE[0x00] through ECMA_TABLE[0x07].
ecma_hasher.update_u64! delegates to update! and returns checksum_u64(), exposing chunked-state and final-checksum behavior not covered by H0.
recommended_action: Add a CRC64 ECMA hasher fuzz target that feeds arbitrary bytes through ecma_hasher.update! and update_u64! using varied chunk partitions, especially total and chunk lengths around 0, 1, 7, 8, 9, and multiples of eight; compare one-shot and partitioned checksum_u64 results and, where possible, check the slicing-by-8 result against an independent byte-at-a-time oracle.
